correctness.rationale: For all odd prime powers with characteristic at least five, normalized projective coordinates give explicit Pascal coefficients and a binary quadratic discriminant. Quadratic character complete-sum identities, with every forbidden coordinate excluded explicitly, yield normalized counts A_sec, A_tan, A_ext. PGL2 transitivity and the free twelve-element hexagon symmetry give the exact per-line multiplicities. All-line exact finite projective enumerations for q=5,7,11,13, normalized enumerations for q=5,7,11,13,17,19,23,29 and F25 reproduce formulas. The infinite claim is proved algebraically, not inferred from experiments; check scripts and observed outputs supplied.

originality.rationale: Compared actual statement implications, not mere title matches. The full accessible 2023 source gives geometric fixed-line fibers and triple-Pascal enumerations, but not their q-specific rational counts. The 2022 source concerns colliding vertices. The published fixed-sextuple Pascal–Kirkman Frobenius analysis does not range over all rational conic sextuples. An existing single q=5 case does not imply the all-field formulas. Residual risk of unindexed equivalent classical finite-geometry enumeration acknowledged.
residual_risks: An older classical or finite-geometry Pascal enumerative table may imply the same formulas but not have been indexed by searches.

value.rationale: The Pascal morphism is a classical, natural enumerative map. The complete arithmetic fiber classification over three line orbits reveals a character-sensitive difference invisible to geometric dimension, recovers the special F5 collapse, and establishes a sharp q7 line-surjectivity threshold for all permitted finite fields. Such a uniform exact image-and-fiber classification is mathematically useful for finite-field hexagram incidence and moduli arithmetic; it is not an arbitrary small-field recomputation.
